title: Is private PAC sample complexity polynomial in VC dimension and log-star Littlestone dimension?
formal: Is there a universal polynomial p such that every finite Boolean concept class C admits a realizable, possibly improper PAC learner using some number $m\le p(1+\mathrm{VC}(C),1+\log^*\mathrm{LD}(C))$ of independent labeled examples, with error at most 1/10 and confidence at least 9/10, while satisfying $(1,1/(100m^2))$-differential privacy? The learning guarantee must hold for every distribution on the domain and every target concept in C. Computation time is unrestricted. Take both dimensions to be at least one; constant classes can be handled separately.
why: The problem seeks a privacy analogue of a foundational characterization theorem in learning theory.

title: Optimal private selection using only Gaussian queries
formal: For a finite set $Y$, public losses $\ell_y$ have sensitivity 1 under a one-record change in the database $X$. The only access to $X$ is through adaptive queries $q_i(X)+N(0,1/(2\rho_i))$, with sensitivity at most 1 and $\sum_i\rho_i\le\rho$. Can the algorithm output $\hat y$ satisfying $\mathbb E[\ell_{\hat y}(X)]-\min_y\ell_y(X)=O(\log|Y|/\sqrt\rho)$?
why: It tests equivalence between two basic privacy primitives. The remaining polyloglogarithmic gap is a concrete obstacle to an optimal reduction.

title: Optimal private selection using only Laplace queries
formal: Let $Y$ be a finite set of candidates, each with a public loss function $\ell_y$ of sensitivity one under a one-record database change. To access the database, an algorithm makes $k$ adaptive sensitivity-1 queries. Its answers are $q_i(X)+\mathrm{Lap}(k)$, where $k$ is the scale. Can it guarantee expected excess loss $O(\log|Y|)$ for arbitrary losses? The algorithm may choose the number of queries.
why: The cost of pure privacy is a structural model distinction, rather than an arbitrary change of constants. It determines the reach of noise addition as a universal primitive.
